explanation:
The restrict keyword in C is a type qualifier applied to pointers that informs the compiler that the pointer is the only means of accessing the object it points to within the scope of the pointer's use. It is used to enable compiler optimizations, such as improved code generation for aliasing scenarios, by assuring that no other pointers or references will access the same memory location, which can lead to faster and more efficient code execution.

The restrict keyword is a type qualifier in C applied to pointers. It informs the compiler that the pointer is the only way to access the object it points to for the duration of its scope. This helps the compiler perform optimizations, such as assuming no aliasing, which can improve performance by reducing unnecessary memory checks.
